subject.title: after_tool_call hook receives a flattened string, not the structured ToolResult — plugins cannot detect exec/bash failures

question: Should OpenClaw canonicalize Codex-native shell/apply_patch `after_tool_call` payloads from app-server completion data instead of forwarding Codex's raw string `PostToolUse` response as the plugin-visible result?
rationale: The bug is source-proven, but the fix changes a public plugin hook payload and must choose between native-relay immediacy, app-server structured fidelity, upstream Codex changes, and duplicate-event avoidance.

options.title: Canonical Structured OpenClaw Payload
options.body: Use app-server commandExecution/file-change completion data as the plugin-visible `after_tool_call` result for Codex-native shell/apply_patch and suppress or replace the raw string event for those tools.

options.title: Wait For Upstream Codex Shape
options.body: Keep OpenClaw relay behavior stable and require Codex to emit structured native shell/exec `tool_response`, accepting that this OpenClaw issue remains blocked until that ships.

options.title: Document Raw String Contract
options.body: Treat Codex native PostToolUse strings as intentional and document that plugins need another surface for exit-code observability.

recommendation.title: Canonical Structured OpenClaw Payload
recommendation.body: Use app-server commandExecution/file-change completion data as the plugin-visible `after_tool_call` result for Codex-native shell/apply_patch and suppress or replace the raw string event for those tools.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision affects the public plugin hook/tool-result API boundary introduced in PR #71021.
